newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi bomb suspect wants to be tried at home - paper.
newsitem.headline: Saudi bomb suspect wants to be tried at home - paper.

text.p: A Saudi suspect in the truck bombing that killed 19 U.S. servicemen in eastern Saudi Arabia has expressed his wish to be tried in his country, a Saudi-owned newspaper reported on Monday.

The London-based al-Hayat reported Hani Abdel-Rahim Hussein al-Sayegh said in an interview from a Canadian prison that he was "confident of his innocence" of Canadian charges he drove a car that gave the go-ahead signal for the bomb-laden truck involved in last June's attack.
"Sayegh reiterated his wish to appear, with guarantees, in front of the judicial authorities in his country to face the charges," al-Hayat said in an Ottawa-datelined article.
"He said he has conveyed his wish to...concerned authorities and hopes to get an answer in the next few days," it added.
It did not say what kind of guarantees Sayegh wanted nor did it say who specifically he had conveyed his wish to.
Saudi Arabia has refused to confirm reports that it has asked for his extradition.
U.S. officials have long sought to question Sayegh about the June 1996 attack on the compound that housed U.S. military personnel in Dhahran in eastern Saudi Arabia.
Canada issued a conditional deportation order against Sayegh on May 14 but has not stipulated where he should go.

The leading candidates are Saudi Arabia and the United States. But if he refuses to give evidence on who was behind the attack it raises the question of whether Washington would want him unless it has an iron-clad case for conviction.

Sayegh -- a 28-year-old Shi'ite Moslem who was arrested in Ottawa on March 18 on the grounds that he posed a security threat to Canada -- has dismissed his lawyer Doug Baum and said he does not want to cooperate with U.S. authorities.
